This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. items.summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.

items.summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

items.summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state

items.summary: Everything needed to redo the two analyses reported in the Technical Note named in the title, and nothing else. What is here the secondary analysis of published length-resolved binding: the contract frozen before any test statistic was computed and its two dated amendments, the resampling of the source's own trimmed-mean procedure, the anchored and anchor-free tests, the post-hoc robustness check across five normalisation variants, the superseded first run kept so the correction stays visible, and the figure generator; the two propositions behind the simulation and the script that checks both against the stored benchmark, per replicate; the simulated measurement study it checks: frozen primary and stress designs, the finite-chain engine, 7,200 simulated datasets under seven observation operators reported as all 302,400 planned rows including the undefined, outside-window and non-identified slots, an independent validator, the stress results, five focused tests, an 83-file manifest and a dependency lock; an 80-value subset of the Source Data for Fig. 2B/C of Sheikh et al., Nat. Commun. 13, 3617 (2022), with its sheet coordinates. These values keep the original article's CC BY 4.0 licence and attribution; the rest of the archive is under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Reproducing The added analysis runs from the archive root with the standard library plus NumPy; the README gives the four commands. It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. Figures redraw with the same layout; their byte sequences depend on which sans-serif face the host has. The base study's own replay script requires bit equality and returns a failure on Linux, where ten of its twenty tables differ in their last digits. What is deliberately not here the manuscript text; the original publisher workbook of Sheikh et al. and every panel of it other than the 80 values used; historical MCMC traces and the exploratory transcript analysis of an earlier, separate study, which this work does not use; correspondence and author-only files. REDACTION.md lists the three files whose description of the work was restated for publication, with the digest before and after; no number, method, decision rule or result changed. Scope Synthetic counts are idealised events, not biological replicates. The site-equivalent pool is not an alpha-dystroglycan molecule count, glycan mass, antibody intensity or muscle force. The published array values are technical replicates of one experiment, and the source states no independent experiments. No real assay's detection ceiling or recovery function is measured anywhere in this archive.

items.summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. items.summary: Everything needed to redo the two analyses reported in the Technical Note named in the title, and nothing else. What is here the secondary analysis of published length-resolved binding: the contract frozen before any test statistic was computed and its two dated amendments, the resampling of the source's own trimmed-mean procedure, the anchored and anchor-free tests, the post-hoc robustness check across five normalisation variants, the superseded first run kept so the correction stays visible, and the figure generator; the two propositions behind the simulation and the script that checks both against the stored benchmark, per replicate; the simulated measurement study it checks: frozen primary and stress designs, the finite-chain engine, 7,200 simulated datasets under seven observation operators reported as all 302,400 planned rows including the undefined, outside-window and non-identified slots, an independent validator, the stress results, five focused tests, an 83-file manifest and a dependency lock; an 80-value subset of the Source Data for Fig. 2B/C of Sheikh et al., Nat. Commun. 13, 3617 (2022), with its sheet coordinates. These values keep the original article's CC BY 4.0 licence and attribution; the rest of the archive is under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Reproducing The added analysis runs from the archive root with the standard library plus NumPy; the README gives the four commands. It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. Figures redraw with the same layout; their byte sequences depend on which sans-serif face the host has. The base study's own replay script requires bit equality and returns a failure on Linux, where ten of its twenty tables differ in their last digits. REDACTION.md lists the three files whose description of the work was restated for publication, with the digest before and after; no number, method, decision rule or result changed. Scope Synthetic counts are idealised events, not biological replicates. The site-equivalent pool is not an alpha-dystroglycan molecule count, glycan mass, antibody intensity or muscle force. The published array values are technical replicates of one experiment, and the source states no independent experiments. No real assay's detection ceiling or recovery function is measured anywhere in this archive.

items.summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol

items.summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Abstract: Classical inferential statistics and p-value hypothesis testing in healthcare big data repositories suffer from severe structural limitations, notably p-hacking, asymptotic N-bias, and the frequent violation of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions due to intra-patient longitudinal dependencies, hospital clustering, and epidemiological shockwaves. To overcome these failures, we introduce an Inverse Breakpoint Analysis, a scale-invariant, physics-inspired metrological audit framework. Our analysis treats discrete clinical event counts not as abstract probabilities, but as physical informational mass. Grounded in Garwood exact discrete limits and Wilson-Hilferty approximations, the framework extends our previous work on stress testing indices for Big health data and establishes three rigorous thresholds: a pure mass saturation limit, a baseline tolerance band, and a structural signal threshold. Through the use of these three parameters, our inverse break-point analysis eliminates false-positive artifacts induced by massive repository sizes while preventing under-powering in small cohorts. Ultimately, the framework demonstrates that percentage-based thresholds are kinematic artifacts of scale, whereas absolute excess discrete mass serves as the sole physical invariant for healthcare data validation. We validated this approach with numerous illustrative examples.

items.summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.

This revision supersedes MSM-25 Rev. 3 and all preceding MSM revisions, except where earlier configurations are explicitly retained as architectural inheritance or documented in the revision-comparison, errata, and reconciliation registers. MSM-26 specifies a cryogenic superconducting architecture whose active core consists of a closed, series-connected chain of Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) fluxonium cells , collectively designated the SNAILonium. Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements possess alternating loop chirality, with each element incorporating exactly (n=3) large Josephson junctions and an associated small Josephson junction. The architecture retains its admissible superconducting conductor configurations, comprising the superconducting flat-wire ribbon and the contour-conformal coplanar-waveguide configuration, with the latter incorporating ground-plane boundaries that follow the SNAIL contour and locally widened gaps around the junction regions. The Josephson-junction interlayer retains three admissible configurations: a conventional dielectric insulating barrier, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and moiré-twisted (MoTe_2). items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. items.summary: The calibration and test probabilities of every run of a tabular classification benchmark, released so that prediction sets and their metrics can be recomputed without refitting a model. A conformal set is a function of four arrays: the class probabilities and labels on a calibration split, and the same on a test split. This deposit is those arrays, together with the software that reads them. The benchmark comprises 218 classification datasets and 22 models from four families, among them 13 tabular foundation models, each evaluated with the same ten seeds. Of the 218, 178 are real datasets and 40 are a synthetic block generated for this benchmark; three of the real ones are Bayesian-network resamplings of small classical datasets and are much larger than their seeds; of those, only one has its own seed in the collection, so that pair is not independent of itself while a rank test treats datasets as independent. Dataset size does not indicate provenance: the largest datasets in the collection are real. Coverage is not uniform and the per-model dataset count is reported for every cell. Eleven datasets carry more than ten classes, and the in-context models measured on them cannot enter them: one refuses and names the limit, another builds a ten-output head and fails inside a kernel. That is a capability limit observed on the models that were run rather than a property claimed of the family, and it is not missing work. One foundation model is measured on the original datasets only. Anything computed across models should be computed on a complete submatrix: the datasets on which every model being compared has all ten seeds. The calibration rows are held out of fitting, of tuning, of early stopping and of the in-context data, and each cell records which rows they were. The code that does it is included, with the line of each step documented. Probabilities are float64 and are not rounded: a prediction set is a comparison against a threshold, and a point sitting on that threshold moves if the value it is compared to is shortened. The data are released under CC BY 4.0. The software included in the source archive is released under the MIT licence, as stated by the LICENSE file it contains. The datasets themselves are not redistributed: each cell carries the row indices into its source dataset, and the synthetic datasets regenerate from their seeds with an included script. Model weights are not redistributed; every checkpoint is named in the model table. Version 1.2.0 adds the runs completed after version 1.1.0 and changes or removes nothing in it. Three new shards (cells-011 to cells-013, 2.02 GB) hold 311 further cells; index.parquet now lists all 46,182 cells and manifest_1016.parquet is their manifest. The files prefixed blocks_1016__ recompute the two blocks outside the main comparison on the completed runs, with the pipeline that produced the article's tables: the large-dataset block on 49 datasets and 21 models (42 in version 1.1.0) and the many-class block on 11 datasets and 7 models (5 in version 1.1.0). The main block of 113 real datasets and 22 models is unchanged. CHANGELOG.md lists what is added and the pairs that are still missing, with the reason for each.

items.summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol

It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. items.summary: This repository contains the data construction and analysis code accompanying a study of recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries. The source history covers July 2013–December 2019. The primary estimation panel covers July 2014–December 2019, allowing a complete preceding-12-month predictor window, and contains 1,650 country-month observations and 58 reactive request-months. The package includes retained source and coding inputs, derived analysis datasets, Python scripts, manuscript tables and figures, and documentation of variable construction and software requirements. Analyses include the primary between–within logistic model, alternative windows and outcomes, country exclusions, leave-one-country-out models, a direct between–within coefficient contrast, separate baseline-covariate adjustments, and calendar-year and outcome-month-inclusive sensitivities. The repository also includes a human-coded external-documentation audit of 22 reactive request-months with zero recorded activity in the preceding 12 months. The audit distinguishes documentation within the same country and window from identification of the outbreak targeted by a particular request. The activity predictor measures recorded active outbreak-months, not case counts or outbreak-to-request delay. Source provenance, coding decisions, and unresolved questions are documented in the package. See README.md for execution instructions.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
items.title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

items.summary: This archive contains workflow code, reduced analysis outputs, plotting inputs, selected simulation intermediates, and checksum manifests associated with the manuscript “Coupled Chemical and Physical Crosslinks in Dry Crosslinked Poly(vinyl alcohol) Networks: A Controlled-Topology Molecular Dynamics Study.” The simulations examine idealized dry poly(vinyl alcohol)–glutaraldehyde networks with controlled covalent strand length and fixed network topology. The archived materials support reproduction of the reported structural, hydrogen-bonding, dihedral-relaxation, segmental-mobility, and high-rate mechanical analyses. Large trajectory files and internal staged crosslink-generation code are not included; the archive treats the generated post-crosslinking LAMMPS data files as fixed inputs for downstream equilibration, conversion, and analysis workflows. The workflow is organized around hydrogel_signac.py , with figure/table provenance documented in MAP_figures.md and file checksums provided in MANIFEST.sha256 .
items.title: Simulation and Analysis Data for Controlled-Topology Dry Crosslinked Poly(vinyl alcohol) Networks

items.summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.
items.title: Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration

items.summary: R code, data and computed output accompanying the manuscript “The Unit-Truncated Power Bilal Distribution: Structural Properties, Shape Analysis, and Statistical Inference” by Preut Thanarat, Tharakorn Jaruruataikant and Nipada Papukdee. The deposit is organised in two parts. round1/ holds the five R scripts of the original submission and their output: the theoretical PDF, CDF and hazard-rate figures; the structural summaries, quantile-based shape measures and entropies; the Monte Carlo study over eight parameter configurations and five sample sizes, including observed-information standard errors and empirical Wald coverage; and the FirmCost and SC16 applications with parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit calibration, the likelihood-ratio test of the nested unit-truncated Bilal restriction, and the CDF, TTT and Q-Q diagnostics. round2/ holds the revision package as it was run. It adds the expanded comparison of nine named model specifications across four source datasets (FirmCost, SC16, AIS and College) and eight analysis groups, with parametric-bootstrap Cramér–von Mises and Anderson–Darling diagnostics at B = 999 and repeated five-fold cross-validation; the College interval-observation likelihood under an assumed nearest-percentage-point rounding mechanism; the limiting-likelihood and boundary-information analysis; the four source datasets together with the archived cross-validation fold assignments, so the predictive comparisons reproduce exactly; and the computed tables and vector figures. A SHA256 manifest is included for verification, and reference/ preserves the original Monte Carlo and goodness-of-fit sources, including the analytic audit of 6,000 replications. All results were produced in R 4.6.1 using the parallel package with a PSOCK cluster and ggplot2 for the figures; the round-two stages also require the sn package. Random seeds, optimizer settings and the boundary-fit classification rule are documented in README.md. Released under the MIT License.
